strings.d1.s0.name: Real Alcázar de Sevilla
strings.d1.s0.tips: A Mudéjar palace (Dorne in Game of Thrones). Don't miss the Hall of Ambassadors and the gardens. Timed tickets must be booked online (buy weeks ahead). First slot is 09:30.
strings.d1.s1.name: Catedral de Sevilla & Giralda
strings.d1.s1.tips: The world's largest Gothic cathedral. Columbus's tomb is here. The Giralda tower has 35 ramps (once ridden up on horseback). Book your ticket online.
strings.d1.s2.name: Barrio Santa Cruz
strings.d1.s2.tips: The former Jewish quarter. Wander the orange-tree squares and Callejón del Agua.
strings.d1.s3.name: Bodega Santa Cruz Las Columnas
strings.d1.s3.tips: A tapas bar where the bill is chalked on the counter. Try the montadito pringá and eat standing up.
strings.d1.s4.name: Plaza de España
strings.d1.s4.tips: The semicircular square built for the 1929 exposition. It has tiled benches for 48 provinces, rowing boats on the canal (6 EUR) and a Star Wars set. Go at sunset.
strings.d1.b0.name: El Rinconcillo
strings.d1.b0.tips: Seville's oldest bar since 1670; try the espinacas con garbanzos (spinach with chickpeas).
strings.d1.b1.name: Casa de Pilatos
strings.d1.b1.tips: A Mudéjar-Renaissance palace with an azulejo tile collection. Go instead of Santa Cruz.
strings.d2.s0.name: Mercado de Triana
strings.d2.s0.tips: The market above San Jorge Castle. It has jamón and tapas stalls, and the Inquisition museum is beneath it.
strings.d2.s1.name: Calle Betis & Triana Ceramics
strings.d2.s1.tips: The riverfront and Centro Cerámica Triana (azulejo museum, 2 EUR). This is the home district of flamenco.
strings.d2.s2.name: Casa Cuesta Triana
strings.d2.s2.tips: An azulejo-tiled bar from 1880. Try the carrillada (braised cheek) and a manzanilla.
strings.d2.s3.name: Metropol Parasol Las Setas
strings.d2.s3.tips: The world's largest wooden structure, known as the "Mushrooms". Watch the sunset from the rooftop walkway. Roman ruins lie below.
strings.d2.s4.name: Flamenco Casa de la Memoria
strings.d2.s4.tips: Intimate courtyard flamenco for 100 people, with guitar, song and dance. Reserve ahead.
strings.d2.b0.name: Tablao Flamenco Los Gallos
strings.d2.b0.tips: A tablao in Santa Cruz since 1966.
strings.d2.b1.name: Bar Las Golondrinas Triana
strings.d2.b1.tips: A tiled bar in Triana; try the solomillo al whisky (pork loin in whisky sauce).
strings.d3.s0.name: Mezquita-Catedral de Córdoba
strings.d3.s0.tips: 45 minutes by AVE. A cathedral sits inside the Umayyad mosque with its 856 columns. Quiet entry is free Monday to Saturday, 08:30–09:30. Look out for the red-and-white arches.
strings.d3.s1.name: Judería & Calleja de las Flores
strings.d3.s1.tips: The Jewish quarter. See the flower-lined alley, the 1315 synagogue and the Maimonides statue.
strings.d3.s2.name: Alcázar de los Reyes Cristianos
strings.d3.s2.tips: The fortress where Columbus met the Catholic Monarchs. It has Roman mosaics and gardens.
strings.d3.s3.name: Bodegas Mezquita Córdoba
strings.d3.s3.tips: Eat salmorejo (thick cold tomato soup) and rabo de toro (oxtail stew).
strings.d3.s4.name: Roman Bridge & Calahorra Tower
strings.d3.s4.tips: A Roman bridge. You get a postcard view of the Guadalquivir and the Mezquita. The Patios festival takes place in May.
strings.d3.b0.name: Palacio de Viana Córdoba
strings.d3.b0.tips: A patio palace with 12 courtyards. Go instead of the Alcázar.
strings.d3.b1.name: Taberna Salinas Córdoba
strings.d3.b1.tips: A tavern from 1879; patio, flamenquín (fried pork roll).
strings.d4.theme: Cartuja, Bullring and Torre del Oro
strings.d4.s0.name: Plaza de Toros de la Maestranza
strings.d4.s0.tips: A Baroque bullring from 1761 with a museum; tour it, and corridas run April to September (controversial).
strings.d4.s1.name: Torre del Oro
strings.d4.s1.tips: An Almohad river tower from 1220. It has a maritime museum and a terrace.
strings.d4.s2.name: Bar Casa Morales
strings.d4.s2.tips: A bar with wine barrels, open since 1850. Next to the cathedral. Try the jamón and a Cruzcampo.
strings.d4.s3.name: Monasterio de la Cartuja CAAC
strings.d4.s3.tips: The monastery where Columbus was buried, later a ceramics factory. It has contemporary art and the Expo 92 island.
strings.d4.s4.name: Guadalquivir Kayak / Paddle
strings.d4.s4.tips: Canoe on the river (under Triana Bridge). Go at sunset.
strings.d4.b0.name: Museo de Bellas Artes de Sevilla
strings.d4.b0.tips: Works by Murillo and Zurbarán in a former convent; on Sundays a painters' market sets up in the square.
strings.d4.b1.name: Eslava
strings.d4.b1.tips: Modern, award-winning tapas. Try the cigarro para Bécquer. In San Lorenzo; expect a queue.
strings.d5.s0.name: Puente Nuevo Ronda
strings.d5.s0.tips: 2 hours by bus (or train plus bus). The 1793 bridge spans the 120 m deep El Tajo gorge. Hemingway's town.
strings.d5.s1.name: Plaza de Toros de Ronda
strings.d5.s1.tips: Spain's oldest bullring (1785). Modern bullfighting was born here. Goya.
strings.d5.s2.name: Casa del Rey Moro Water Mine
strings.d5.s2.tips: A Moorish water mine with 231 steps down into the gorge. The gardens are also worth a look.
strings.d5.s3.name: Bardal Ronda / Tragatá
strings.d5.s3.tips: Benito Gómez's tapas bar (a Michelin-starred chef). Try the rabo de toro (oxtail).
strings.d5.s4.name: Mirador de Ronda & Alameda
strings.d5.s4.tips: A cliffside garden with views of the Serranía mountains. Head back at 17:00.
strings.d5.b0.name: Baños Árabes Ronda
strings.d5.b1.name: Bar Cuevas del Sol Setenil
strings.d5.b1.tips: Tapas in a white village carved beneath the rock. 20 minutes from Ronda (by car or tour).
strings.d6.s0.name: Cádiz Cathedral & Torre Tavira
strings.d6.s0.tips: 1.5 hours by train. Europe's oldest city (Phoenician, 1100 BC). It has a golden-domed cathedral and a camera obscura in the Tavira tower.
strings.d6.s1.name: Mercado Central de Cádiz
strings.d6.s1.tips: A fish market and "rincón gastronómico" (food corner). Try tortillitas de camarones (shrimp fritters).
strings.d6.s2.name: Barrio de la Viña
strings.d6.s2.tips: The carnival and fishermen's quarter. The February Carnival is Spain's most famous.
strings.d6.s3.name: Playa de la Caleta
strings.d6.s3.tips: A city beach between two castles (the Bond film with Halle Berry). Swim and watch the fishing boats.
strings.d6.s4.name: El Faro de Cádiz
strings.d6.s4.tips: A seafood restaurant open since 1964. Try the frito gaditano (Cádiz fried fish). Return train at 18:00.
strings.d6.b0.name: Jerez de la Frontera Tío Pepe
strings.d6.b0.tips: A sherry bodega tour with tasting and Andalusian horses. Go instead of Cádiz (1 hour by train).
strings.d6.b1.name: Freiduría Las Flores Cádiz
strings.d6.b1.tips: Fried fish in a paper cone. Eat standing up.
strings.d7.s0.name: Basílica de la Macarena
strings.d7.s0.tips: The Weeping Virgin (star of Semana Santa). The treasury museum costs 5 EUR. Roman walls are nearby too.
strings.d7.s1.name: Alameda de Hércules
strings.d7.s1.tips: A bohemian square with Hercules columns. It has plenty of cafés.
strings.d7.s2.name: Mercado de Feria Breakfast
strings.d7.s2.tips: Seville's oldest market. Have a tostada con tomate y jamón (toast with tomato and ham) and say your goodbyes.
strings.d7.s3.name: Casa de Pilatos Gate & Calle Sierpes Souvenirs
strings.d7.s3.tips: Fans and azulejo souvenirs. On Sierpes.
strings.d7.s4.name: Santa Justa Airport Bus EA
strings.d7.s4.tips: The airport bus takes 35 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Confitería La Campana
strings.d7.b0.tips: A pastry shop from 1885. Try the torrijas (Spanish French toast) and yemas (sweet egg-yolk confections).
strings.d7.b1.name: Iglesia de San Luis de los Franceses
strings.d7.b1.tips: The most ornate Baroque church. Go instead of Macarena.
strings.note0: The centre is walkable. Tram/bus costs 1.40 EUR, and Sevici bikes are available. The EA airport bus is 4 EUR. Córdoba is 45 min by AVE, Cádiz 1.5 hours, Ronda 2 hours by bus.
strings.note1: SUMMER hits 40–45°C (Europe's oven): sightsee between 09:00 and 12:00 and after 19:00, and take a siesta at midday. Go to the Alcázar in the first slot and Plaza de España at sunset. In August the city is empty.
strings.note2: Alcázar 15 EUR, online booking REQUIRED (buy weeks ahead). Cathedral 13 EUR, online. Tapas 3–4 EUR, set menu 15, flamenco 22–35. Round up your tip.
strings.note3: Tapas culture: eat standing up, visit 2–3 bars, and order "tapa/media/ración". Lunch is at 14:00, dinner after 21:00. Try salmorejo, espinacas, pringá and carrillada.
strings.note4: Flamenco: Casa de la Memoria (intimate), La Carbonería (free, late at night), Triana peñas (flamenco clubs).
strings.note5: The fruit of the orange trees is bitter (used for marmalade). Don't eat it.
